name: The Robert-Brasseur Chestnut
verified_sources: https://wms.inspire.geoportail.lu/geoserver/ogc/features/v1/collections/ps:PS.Remarkable_trees/items?f=text/csv (INSPIRE geoportal export of the official register, entry Luxembourg - LF de la Ville Haute, id remarkable_trees.134, coordinate 49.612987/6.131524, legal basis Reglement grand-ducal du 31 janvier 2025 etablissant la liste des arbres remarquables, legilux.public.lu/eli/etat/leg/rgd/2025/01/31/a40/jo)

https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q16763933 (structured record citing the same regulation, register no. 134, perimeter 4.3m, height 23.5m, crown diameter 1.37m; carries two independently dated Commons field photographs, Jan 2008 and Jan 2024: Special:FilePath/Käschtebam R Brasseur Lëtzebuerg 1.jpg and Special:FilePath/Luxembourg, marronnier remarquable Square Robert-Brasseur (104).jpg)
access: Free, in a public city square (Ville-Haute); open at all times, no restriction found.
transport: Central Luxembourg City; walkable from the city centre (Place Guillaume II / Hamilius area). Exact walk time not verified this pass.
verify_notes: Officially designated a remarkable tree under Luxembourg's Reglement grand-ducal du 31 janvier 2025 (in force since 15 Feb 2025), which legally protects it from felling/uprooting/damage without ministerial authorisation. The INSPIRE geoportal CSV point for this designation (id remarkable_trees.134, Luxembourg - LF de la Ville Haute) sits within about 1.5m of the Wikidata coordinate, i.e. the same individual tree. Wikidata gives perimeter (girth) 4.3m = 430cm, height 23.5m, crown diameter 4.12m (its 'diameter' field of 1.37m is trunk diameter derived from the girth, not crown). No age is recorded anywhere found this pass; flagging so the page can ask the reader. CAVEAT ON SOURCING: both sources ultimately trace to the same 2025 designation process (the CSV is the government's own geodata export of the regulation; the Wikidata measurements cite the same regulation as their reference), so this is not two fully independent documentary sources in the strictest sense, though the CSV (government geodata) and the Wikidata/Commons record (separately maintained platform, with two field photographs predating and postdating the regulation) are institutionally and editorially separate. Flagged for that reason rather than for any doubt about the tree's existence or species, both of which are visually obvious from the photographs. A local geoview.info listing independently gives circumference 1.30m and height 23m for a chestnut at this same square, which does not match the Wikidata girth of 4.3m; that figure was NOT used (source not directly verified/fetched, appears to be a much smaller specimen measurement or a unit error) but is noted here in case a future pass can resolve the discrepancy.

name: The Bastion Beck Beech

location.address: Bastion Beck, Place de la Constitution, Ville-Haute, Luxembourg City

verified_sources: https://wms.inspire.geoportail.lu/geoserver/ogc/features/v1/collections/ps:PS.Remarkable_trees/items?f=text/csv (INSPIRE geoportal export of the official register, entry Luxembourg - LF de la Ville Haute, id remarkable_trees.128, coordinate 49.609128/6.127750, legal basis Reglement grand-ducal du 31 janvier 2025 etablissant la liste des arbres remarquables)

https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q13101832 (structured record, register no. 128, perimeter 4.12m, height 22.7m; Commons field photo 'Buch Bastioun Beck 01.jpg' whose own caption notes the Gëlle Fra monument is visible through the crown, confirming the specific viewpoint)
access: Free, on Place de la Constitution / Bastion Beck, one of the city's best-known public viewpoints (the Gëlle Fra war memorial stands here); open at all times.
transport: Central Luxembourg City, on the Boulevard Roosevelt side of Ville-Haute overlooking the Petrusse valley; walkable from the city centre. Exact walk time not verified this pass.
verify_notes: Officially designated a remarkable tree under the same 31 January 2025 regulation as lux_001 (register no. 128). The INSPIRE CSV point sits within about 1.5m of the Wikidata coordinate. Perimeter 4.12m (412cm), height 22.7m. Species is Fagus sylvatica (Wikidata P10241 -> Q146149, European beech); the German/Luxembourgish label 'Rotbuche'/'Buch' distinguishes it from the copper/purple-leaved cultivar (Blutbuche/hêtre pourpre) seen elsewhere in the city (a separate designated tree near Saint Michael's Church on the Corniche, not delivered this pass, was checked and is a different, purple-leaved specimen). Stands at Bastion Beck / Place de la Constitution, arguably the single most-visited viewpoint in the city (the Gëlle Fra monument and the panoramic view over the fortifications and Petrusse valley). No age recorded anywhere found this pass; flag for the reader. Same sourcing caveat as lux_001: both sources trace to the same 2025 designation, so treat as one register source plus a separately maintained photographic/structured record rather than two fully independent documents.

Exact street address not pinned down within the 40-minute window; coordinates place it on the escarpment/Corniche side of Ville-Haute above the historic Pfaffenthal quarter, within a few hundred metres of lux_001 and lux_002, so it joins the same walkable cluster. name: The Krombach Oak
verified_sources: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Luxembourg,_ch%C3%AAne_Krombach,_parc_Louvigny_(101).jpg (independent field photograph by Commons contributor GilPe, dated 3 January 2020, caption: 'le chene Krombach plante en memoire du botaniste Jean-Henri-Guillaume Krombach (1791-1881)', geotagged in Parc Louvigny)

https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q13103645 (structured record: species Quercus robur, named after Jean-Henri-Guillaume Krombach (Q3460050), a point-in-time value of 1875 whose exact meaning is not confirmed, see note)
access: Free, in Parc Louvigny, a public city park in Ville-Haute; open at all times, no restriction found.
transport: Central Luxembourg City, Ville-Haute, near Villa Louvigny; walkable from the city centre. Exact walk time not verified this pass.
verify_notes: NOT found in the 31 January 2025 official register CSV (no INSPIRE point within several hundred metres, and the Wikidata record carries no register-id property unlike lux_001/002/003), so this one rests on two independent non-register sources instead: a geotagged Commons field photograph (GilPe, 2020) and Wikidata's structured record. Both agree it is an oak (chene) in Parc Louvigny planted or dedicated in memory of Jean-Henri-Guillaume Krombach, a Luxembourg pharmacist and botanist (1791-1881). Wikidata carries a 'point in time' value of 1875, which would make the tree about 150 years old if it is a planting date, but the property used (P585) does not clearly mean 'planted' rather than some other event date (e.g. when the memorial naming happened), and no source seen this pass states 'planted in 1875' outright. Treating that date as an age would be exactly the bridge-claim trap the brief warns about, so age_estimate is left empty and the date is flagged here for the writer/reader instead. Species confirmed as Quercus robur via Wikidata taxon claim; visually an oak in both photographs. Girth and height not found this pass.
